comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C2, C3, C33-C35, C54-C56, C59) about PMA enhancing Wnt signaling. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED across multiple systems, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting the finding is interesting in Xenopus but requesting additional mammalian/cancer cell validation beyond HEK293 cells and calling for mechanistic clarification.

Both address PMA-Wnt synergy dependence on macropinocytosis and lysosomal function. OpenEval (C4, C36, C37, C57, C60-C62) and peer review (C4, C36, C57, C6, C37, C58, C60) largely overlap. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers describing the analyses as 'compelling' and providing 'compelling evidence' for the link.

Partial overlap on macropinocytosis induction claims. OpenEval R13 (C63, C64) finds SUPPORTED evidence that PMA stimulates macropinocytosis in CRC cells. Peer R3 includes these claims plus C61, C62, rating UNCERTAIN due to concerns that SW480 data don't directly address Wnt signaling role and requesting validation in additional cell lines.

Strong agreement on temporal requirement claims (C40, C66-C68). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the bidirectional order-of-addition experiments provide strong evidence for timing requirements. Peer reviewers found analyses 'compelling' with no concerns raised about these temporal experiments.

Substantial overlap on Rac1 requirement for Wnt signaling. OpenEval R3 (C5, C6, C38, C69-C73) and peer R5 (C5, C38, C70-C78) both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note connections between components 'remain unclear' mechanistically but do not dispute individual findings. Peer R5 also includes Rac1 stabilization claims (C76-C78) from OpenEval R10.

Perfect agreement on membrane trafficking requirement for downstream components (C41-C44). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the requirement is somewhat unexpected for β-catenin. Peer reviewers found conclusions compelling with no questions raised.

Perfect agreement on CRC tissue array correlations (C7, C45-C47, C81-C83, C85). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is correlative, not causal. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'compelling' and a 'novel link' of interest to tumor biologists.

Strong agreement on GSK3 decrease with cancer progression (C8, C48, C86, C89). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with GSK3 sequestration model. Peer reviewers found analyses compelling with no disputes about the findings.

High overlap on Tes localization regulation by Wnt (C49, C50, C93-C95). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the SW480/SW480APC genetic comparison. Peer reviewers found analyses compelling and accept the demonstration of Wnt-dependent trafficking of focal adhesion components.

Partial overlap on FAK requirement for Wnt signaling. OpenEval R11 (C97, C98) finds SUPPORTED evidence across systems. Peer R10 includes these plus C99, C100, also rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'novel link' while noting mechanistic connections 'remain unclear.'

OpenEval R12 (C99, C100) addresses PMA effects requiring macropinocytosis/lysosomal activity in CRC cells, finding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these claims with C97, C98, also rating SUPPORTED and acknowledging the novel link between pathways.

Perfect agreement on xenograft validation (C88). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this confirms generalizability of tissue array findings. Peer reviewers found analyses compelling with no questions raised.

OpenEval R9 (C74, C75) addresses Rac1 inhibition effects in 3D spheroid cultures, finding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R5 includes these claims within a broader evaluation (C5, C38, C70-C78) also rated SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers finding analyses 'compelling.'

OpenEval R10 (C76-C78) demonstrates Wnt signaling increases Rac1 levels, finding evidence SUPPORTED and noting a positive feedback loop. Peer R5 includes these claims in a broader Rac1 evaluation, also rating SUPPORTED with compelling analyses noted.
OpenEval R15 evaluates background claims about PMA (C1, C9, C10, C32) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual/background claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates extensive background claims about Wnt signaling and GSK3 regulation (C12-C23, C25) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual/background claims.
